title: Deterministic framing and idempotent tool-call contracts for interleaved streaming
creator: Anika Patel
description: PRD-level acceptance criteria for StructuredOutputV2: introduce deterministic framing for interleaved streamed JSON + tool-invocation payloads, a checkpointing handshake for recovery, and explicit idempotency and retry semantics for function/tool calls emitted mid-stream. This ticket clarifies scope boundaries, error-mode categories, SDK requirements, and telemetry hooks required for rollout.
scope: Define a minimal wire-format for framed events (FRAME_START, FRAME_CHUNK, FRAME_END) compatible with current streaming APIs
Specify schema version negotiation (v1/v2) and soft downgrade behavior when runtime lacks v2 support
Design a checkpoint token emitted at frame boundaries for client rehydration and tool-call replay
Define idempotency token semantics for tool calls and a canonical retry policy for transient failures
Document observable events (frame-ack, frame-lost, tool-invoke-status) and required metrics/log fields
Enumerate SDK contract changes for Node/Python to parse frames, surface partial objects, and expose recovery helpers
out_of_scope: Full binary framing (we remain text/utf-8 only)
New transport protocols other than existing SSE/websocket/http-streaming
Automatic server-side side-effect replay beyond tool invocation acknowledgement window
acceptance_criteria: Wire-format: Each streamed message must be one framed event with a stable header containing: schema_version, frame_id (uuid), seq_index (int), frame_type in {FRAME_START, FRAME_CHUNK, FRAME_END, TOOL_CALL, HEARTBEAT}, and optional checkpoint_token. SDKs must deserialize header without blocking on body parsing.

Schema negotiation: If client requests schema_version=2 and server responds with 1, server must continue streaming flagged with a 'compatibility_warning' frame within first 2 frames and fall back to documented v1 behavior. SDK must provide a 'compatibility_mode' flag to surface this to callers.

Checkpointing: On every FRAME_END the runtime must emit a checkpoint_token stable across retries for the same logical response. Clients using the checkpoint_token to rehydrate must be able to resume from the next frame after checkpoint_token without replaying earlier frames. End-to-end test: simulate mid-stream disconnect and verify resume succeeds within 30s using checkpoint_token.

Tool-call idempotency: Every TOOL_CALL frame must include tool_call_id and idempotency_token. The runtime guarantees that the same tool_call_id combined with idempotency_token will not result in duplicate side effects when retried within the tool-call window (default 120s). Cross-check: mocked tool endpoint should see at most one invocation for repeated resume attempts with identical tokens.

Partial-object validity: Clients must be able to incrementally validate and reconstruct JSON objects emitted across multiple FRAME_CHUNK frames; acceptance test: SDK incremental reassembly returns parseable partial objects at each FRAME_CHUNK boundary and final object equals canonical JSON emitted server-side.

Backpressure and HEARTBEAT: If client registers explicit backpressure (via HTTP/WS flow control) the runtime must pause emitting new FRAME_START events and send HEARTBEAT frames every 1s until resume. Test: apply simulated slow consumer and validate no FRAME_START is emitted while backpressure is asserted and HEARTBEATs continue.

Failure classification and fallback: Define three error classes emitted as ERROR frames: recoverable_transient (retryable by client/server), deterministic_schema_violation (fatal for this stream, server must emit an ERROR with human-readable diagnostics), and tool_side_effect_unconfirmed (requires canonical retry policy). Acceptance: fault injection must produce correct ERROR frame and SDK surfaces error_code and suggested_action fields.

Observability: Every frame must include trace_id and optional span_id. Runtime must emit metrics: frames_emitted, frames_retransmitted, checkpoint_resumes, tool_calls_inflight, tool_calls_retried. Dashboards should show these metrics per-model and per-route. Test: replay a recorded session and verify metrics increment as expected.

Compatibility testing: Regression suite must include mixed workloads with: short chat responses, long-form streaming with multiple tool calls, and interleaved embeddings+tool frames. All suites pass with <1% framing error rate on CI under synthetic packet loss (simulate 0.5% packet drop).

SDK ergonomics: Provide high-level helpers: StreamReader.resume(checkpoint_token), StreamReader.onToolCall(callback) with built-in ack(token), and StreamReader.replayToolCall(tool_call_id, idempotency_token) returning canonical outcome. Unit tests for Node and Python confirm API contracts and error propagation semantics.
definition_of_done: Spec reviewed and signed off by runtime, SDK, and security leads
ENG implementation PR with unit and integration tests merged
Node/Python SDKs updated with helper APIs and tests
Documentation: Console docs, API reference, and migration guide published
Observability: Grafana dashboards and logs indexing configured
Security review completed for idempotency tokens and KMS handling
notes: Trade-offs: We prefer a textual framed protocol to avoid transport-level compatibility issues with existing customers. Binary would be more efficient but adds SDK complexity.
Scope change request: initially included server-side automatic tool-call replay; pushed to follow-up because it requires per-customer policy controls and audit logging expansion.
Risk: Idempotency token storage increases state; propose TTL of 5 minutes and storage sharding per-route. Engineering asked to validate memory impact for high-throughput routes.
Migration: For existing v1 streams we will add a transitional 'compatibility_warning' frame and deprecate v1 behavior after two quarters with telemetry-based rollback criteria.
